selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main quality does the passage say can be seen in everything, from the whole universe down to small parts of the human body?
questions.answer: A careful and wise order can be seen in all of them.

questions.question: Which large pattern of the earth is mentioned as an example of this order?
questions.answer: Its daily and yearly turning.

questions.question: Why does the passage deny that anything else can creatively interfere with things?
questions.answer: Because true creative control belongs only to the One with complete power and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about purpose and benefit in creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that order is set for meaningful goals and useful results.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from this beneficial order?
questions.answer: The One who creates and manages all beings is one and acts intentionally.

questions.question: What do the many examples of “one” in the world lead the reader to understand?
questions.answer: They lead the reader to understand that the Master of the world is one.

questions.question: What are some examples of “oneness” given in the world?
questions.answer: The lamp is one, the time-marker is one, the sponge is one, the cook is one, the drink is one, and the field is one.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the servants used to care for living beings?
questions.answer: They are many great and high-ranking servants.

questions.question: What is one attribute named in the passage besides wisdom?
questions.answer: Mercy or grace.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example where giving life appears along with creating, shaping, and providing?
questions.answer: One action in a thing is tied to many others, all working together from one source.

questions.question: What idea is repeated through the passage from the largest things to the smallest?
questions.answer: Everything shows a planned order.

questions.question: What are two small human examples of order mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: A person’s face and the movement of blood cells.

questions.question: What kind of being is able to act on things intentionally and creatively?
questions.answer: Only the One with absolute power and absolute wisdom.

questions.question: Why are knowledge and wisdom linked to arranging things for benefits?
questions.answer: Because useful arrangement needs understanding of what is best.

questions.question: What does the passage say this world-order proves about the Creator and Manager of beings?
questions.answer: It proves that He is one and acts by will and choice.

questions.question: Why does the passage list many “one” examples in the world?
questions.answer: To strengthen the proof that the world has one Maker.

questions.question: Who are the “guests” in this hospice picture?
questions.answer: The living creatures in the world.

questions.question: What character trait of the Maker is shown by serving living guests through many great servants?
questions.answer: His great generosity and hospitality.

questions.question: What does the passage say about where these Names and actions are found?
questions.answer: Their signs are found in every part of the world.

questions.question: Why is the example of Quickener important for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that life is given together with creating, shaping, and providing in one coordinated act.

questions.question: What does the first paragraph teach about the universe and the human body?
questions.answer: Both show a detailed order set by wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say no one besides the Absolutely Powerful and Absolutely Wise can do?
questions.answer: No one else can purposely and creatively control any thing.

questions.question: How does the passage describe all other things besides that One?
questions.answer: They receive what is done to them, show His works, and do not act on their own.

questions.question: What is needed for arranging things toward goals and benefits?
questions.answer: Knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice are needed.
